title: POC scoping - benchmark harness integration

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 mins | Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Gomez (Solutions), Maya Chen (Acadia ML), Tom Ruiz (Acadia Platform), Priya Nand (Acadia CTO)

Summary (auto): quick scoping for benchmark integration and success criteria; decide on streaming vs non-streaming tests; identify data and infra constraints; agree timeline.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call — we've got Raj and Nina from our side, and Maya, Tom, Priya from Acadia. does that match?
[00:08] Maya Chen: Yep that's right, thanks Lena.
[00:11] Tom Ruiz: yeh, all good here.
[00:13] Priya Nand: hi all.
[00:16] Lena: Great. The goal for today is to scope the POC for benchmark planning and harness integration — specifically we want to agree success criteria, workload sizing, and whether to run streaming versus non-streaming tests. We'll also cover timelines and next steps.
[00:34] Raj Patel: I'll jump in on the technical bits — we want to understand your request shapes, concurrency, token lengths, and the client-side harness you use so we can make the runs reproducible.
[00:45] Maya: yep — quick context, we have a clinical summarization feature running in prod, roughly 35 rps at peak, avg prompt length is 600 tokens, response avg 450 tokens, but there's a long tail up to 2k when summaries include long histories. We currently use an internal harness built on k6 but with some custom streaming stubs; it's a bit brittle.
[01:10] Tom: we also care about latency P95 under 500ms for interactive flows, but cost per 1k tokens matters since volume will scale. for the backend batch jobs latency can be higher.
[01:26] Lena: helpful. So for the POC we typically run two phases: a functional correctness and quality check (samples + metrics), then a performance baseline with isolated configs. For the benchmark harness integration we can accept k6 traces or a simple Python harness — we can also run our own load generator if you prefer.
[01:47] Maya: we prefer to reuse our trace-based approach so numbers reflect real shapes. can you ingest k6 scripts?
[01:53] Raj: absolutely — we can take k6 JS scenarios. if you have streaming via chunked SSE or websocket we have a streaming harness; it expects a stub that replays chunk timings. there might be some fragility with live streaming in our infra so we'll surface that.
[02:10] Priya: is there a big difference in measurement between streaming and non-streaming? we heard streaming looks faster to the user but is harder to measure.
[02:19] Raj: right — streaming reduces time-to-first-token which users perceive as faster. from a server perspective it changes how you measure per-request cost because connection time and incremental token emission matter. it's tricky to compare apples-to-apples unless you define the exact UX metric: TTF token vs total completion time vs tokens/sec throughput.
[02:38] Lena: for the success criteria let's try to be explicit: Customer wants P95 latency <= 500ms for interactive flows and cost-per-1k-tokens under X (we'll have to confirm X offline). We should also validate model quality with a small eval set — like pass rate on a rubric (we'll do side-by-side sample evals).
[02:57] Maya: agreed. For cost target, we're thinking of keeping it at or below our current infra spend per inference; I'll pull a number.
[03:05] Tom: also we need to ensure that sensitive PHI never leaves the VPC in the Private deployment — what are your options for Private or Dedicated?
[03:15] Lena: good question. We have Hosted, Dedicated, and Redwood Private. For this POC we can run on Hosted with redactions in the harness (masking) or we can provision a dedicated pool or Private VPC if you want to test egress controls. For POC speed we usually start on hosted with scrubbed traces then move to dedicated/private for final validation.
[03:34] Maya: OK that'll work, we'll scrub traces first.
[03:37] Raj: about harness integration — two main paths: 1) you provide k6 scripts and replay traces against our endpoint, we capture metrics; 2) we run a captured workload replay inside your infra via a peered test runner (VPC) to replicate network conditions. Path 2 helps if you have strict networking.
[03:56] Priya: Path 2 sounds better for compliance but slower to set up. how long to spin up a peered test runner?
[04:03] Raj: typically 2-3 days for the networking setup if firewall rules and peering approvals are ready; otherwise it can be longer.
[04:12] Lena: We'll provide a benchmark template that includes the measurement spec: metrics we capture (P50/P95/P99 latencies, time-to-first-byte/token, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU util, cost per 1k tokens), and an example k6 scenario.
[04:29] Maya: for our long-tail requests — how do you handle requests that hit 2k tokens, do you shard or chunk?
[04:37] Raj: we stream tokens as they're generated — no implicit sharding. for benchmarks we can include a mixed workload with percentiles of request sizes so the baseline reflects real mix. also we have options for quantized models to lower cost but might affect quality.
[04:55] Tom: can Redwood run quantized models in Dedicated or Private? we need to know if quantization is supported with existing model variants.
[05:02] Lena: yes, we recommend quantized variants for cost-sensitive workloads; our runtime supports int8 and some 4-bit pathways depending on the model. we'll include model variant recommendations in the deck.
[05:12] Maya: another practical question: our client uses streaming SSE and monitors the stream for partials. how do you recommend simulating network jitter and chunk delays?
[05:22] Raj: our streaming harness accepts a timing profile: inter-chunk delays and sizes. if you can export a sample of real chunk timings we can replay them. otherwise we can approximate with synthetic jitter parameters.
[05:35] Priya: OK. timeline—what's realistic? we want baseline numbers quickly.
[05:40] Lena: Proposed timeline: send benchmark template and harness instructions by Fri (2026-03-06). Customer shares traces and k6 scripts by Mon (2026-03-09). Redwood runs a dry run and shares baseline results by 2026-03-13. Then schedule a 1-hour call week of 2026-03-16 to review and decide whether to move to dedicated/private validation. Does that align?
[06:02] Tom: yes that aligns.
[06:05] Maya: sounds good.
[06:08] Raj: a couple of measurement caveats: for streaming tests our time-to-first-token metric requires synchronized clocks or markers in the trace; otherwise the replay can shift timings. we usually insert an epoch marker in the harness.
[06:22] Lena: noted. we'll include instructions for markers in the template.
[06:26] Maya: security: we need SOC2 stuff, audit logs, SSO, KMS integration—what's available for POC?
[06:35] Lena: we can share our security pack — SOC2 type II report, details on RBAC and SAML SSO, KMS integration for Private deployments. For the initial hosted POC we'll provide a document and temporary isolated keys; for deeper auditability we run Dedicated/Private.
[06:52] Priya: please include retention settings too.
[06:55] Lena: will do.
[06:58] Tom: ok, about metrics collection — do you ingest GPU metrics or do we need to push them?
[07:05] Raj: for Hosted we'll provide aggregate GPU util and model profiling from our side. for Dedicated/Private we can install a small exporter in the node to push Prometheus metrics; we'll include the runbook.
[07:17] Maya: good. let's talk pass/fail criteria for the POC — what does success look like?
[07:22] Lena: success criteria proposed: 1) P95 latency for interactive route <= 500ms on your 90% traffic mix; 2) cost per 1k tokens within target (TBD); 3) no data exfil observed in network checks; 4) evaluation quality meets rubric (>=X pass rate). we can refine numeric thresholds once you share baseline numbers.
[07:45] Priya: agreed to start with those high-level criteria.
[07:49] Raj: Another thing: for the baseline runs we should isolate variables — run same model variant on Redwood with the same tokenization and prompt pre-processing. small differences in tokenization can skew cost and latency.
[08:03] Maya: yes we use sentencesplitter v2 which changes token counts; we'll export token counts per request.
[08:09] Lena: perfect. On the harness: can you share an example k6 script now? even a sanitized one is fine so we can validate parsing.
[08:19] Maya: I'll upload to the shared drive after the call.
[08:23] Tom: one more practical — can Redwood produce a CSV of per-request timing and tokens so we can run our own analysis?
[08:30] Raj: yes we export per-request JSON/CSV with timestamps, token counts, and model variant. for streaming we include chunk timings.
[08:39] Maya: wonderful.
[08:41] Lena: Great — let's capture a few edge cases to include in the harness: a) 2k token long-tail requests, b) many small requests (<=50 tokens) to validate batching, c) streaming partials test with jitter, and d) a batch job workload (high tokens/batch).
[09:00] Priya: OK. Any blockers from your side?
[09:03] Maya: only that we need to sanitize PHI before sending traces — that might add a day.
[09:08] Tom: we may need a security review ticket for VPC peering; I'll open one today.
[09:13] Lena: good — we'll attach security docs in the follow-up.
[09:17] Raj: Implementation detail — for cost measurement we want to ensure you include all overheads: prompt tokens, response tokens, and egress costs. clarify what you mean by cost per 1k tokens.
[09:29] Maya: we'll include the infra baseline numbers; we'll accept Redwood's reported per-token cost and reconcile it after.
[09:35] Lena: repeat of next steps: we'll send the benchmark template and example k6 script + streaming stub by 2026-03-06. you (Maya) will scrub and share traces and k6 scripts by 2026-03-09. Raj will prepare runbook and initial infra suggestion by 2026-03-06. We'll run a baseline and share results by 2026-03-13 and meet week of 2026-03-16 to review.
[09:58] Priya: sounds actionable.
[10:00] Maya: thank you, appreciate the clarity.
[10:03] Tom: thanks everyone.
[10:05] Lena: quick note — any competitors in play? Maya earlier mentioned they did a quick eval vs Anthropic and OpenAI. are there any active procurement steps?
[10:15] Priya: not yet — just exploratory but we want concrete numbers before deciding.
[10:20] Lena: understood. last question — do you want Redwood to run the harness from our cloud region (us-west) or your peered region?
[10:28] Tom: let's start with us-west for speed and then replicate in our peered region if needed.
[10:34] Lena: perfect. Thanks all — we'll follow up with the template and docs.
[10:39] Meeting end.

Auto sections (optional):
Questions:
- Do you support direct replay of k6 streaming stubs? Answer: Yes with timing profile.
- How long to spin up peered runner? Answer: 2-3 business days typically.
